summary.text: There are three plans: Escalating, Standard and Basic. Choose based on how willing you are to adjust your lifestyle as costs rise.

details.heading: Escalating Plan
details.body: Consider this plan if you are worried about rising living costs. Payouts start lower, then grow by 2% every year for life. This generally helps you maintain your retirement lifestyle.

details.heading: Standard Plan
details.body: This plan gives steady payouts that start higher than the Escalating Plan. The payouts do not grow with inflation, so you may need to lower your lifestyle as costs rise.

details.heading: Basic Plan
details.body: This plan starts with lower monthly payouts, which will be lower later on. Payouts will get lower when your combined CPF balances eventually fall below $60,000.

details.heading: What all three plans provide
details.body: All three plans provide payouts for as long as you live. Your premiums earn risk-free CPF interest rates. Any remaining CPF LIFE premium balance goes to your beneficiaries, together with your remaining CPF savings, when you pass on.

sources.page_title: What are the CPF LIFE plans available and which is the right plan for me?

quotes.text: There are three CPF LIFE plans to choose from – Escalating Plan, Standard Plan and Basic Plan.
If you are worried about the rising costs of living, you can consider the Escalating Plan which provides monthly payouts that start lower initially but grow by 2% every year for life.
If you are willing to live a more modest lifestyle and buy less as years pass, you may find the Standard Plan which provides steady payouts suitable for you.
If you don’t mind starting with lower monthly payouts which will be lower later on, then the Basic Plan is good enough.

In all three plans, you will enjoy payouts no matter how long you live, your premiums will enjoy risk-free CPF interest rates, and any remaining CPF LIFE premium balance will be given to your beneficiaries, together with your remaining CPF savings when you pass on.

title.full: How CPF LIFE Basic Plan works

summary.text: The Basic Plan gives lifelong payouts. They may fall as your CPF balances drop below $60,000.

details.heading: How payments work
details.body: Your monthly payouts are paid for as long as you live. The Basic Plan pays from your Retirement Account savings until age 90. After that, payments come from your CPF LIFE premium.

details.heading: Your CPF LIFE premium
details.body: When you join CPF LIFE, about 10% to 20% of your Retirement Account savings becomes your CPF LIFE premium. The premium continues to earn CPF interest, which is included in your payouts.

details.heading: Why payouts can fall
details.body: Your Retirement Account savings continue to earn 4% interest. You may also earn extra interest on the first $60,000 of your CPF balances. As your balances fall below $60,000, that extra interest decreases, so your payouts can gradually become lower.

details.heading: After you pass away
details.body: Your remaining CPF LIFE premium balance will be paid to your beneficiaries.

For the CPF LIFE Basic Plan, your CPF LIFE monthly payouts will first be paid from your RA savings until age 90. Thereafter, you will receive the monthly payout from your CPF LIFE premium.
New CPF LIFE members: When you join CPF LIFE, about 10% to 20% of your Retirement Account (RA) savings will be used as your CPF LIFE premium.
As your RA savings are gradually withdrawn to provide you with monthly payouts, the extra interest you earn will decrease when the total balances fall below $60,000.
Upon your passing, your remaining CPF LIFE premium balance will be paid to your beneficiaries.

quotes.text: CareShield Life, ElderShield, MediShield Life, CPF LIFE, CHAS, HCG, PioneerDAS, ElderFund and IDAPE are schemes that help Singaporeans with different types of healthcare and retirement expenses.

CareShield Life and ElderShield are long-term care insurance schemes that will provide Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with some financial protection should one develop severe disability (i.e. unable to perform at least three or more of the six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)), especially in old age.
CPF LIFE is the national longevity insurance annuity scheme, which insures Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents against the risk of outliving their retirement savings.

Home Caregiving Grant (HCG) is a monthly cash grant of $200 to support families caring for loved ones with permanent moderate disability (i.e. always require some assistance with at least three Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)) who reside in the community.

ElderFund is a discretionary government assistance scheme providing monthly cash assistance of up to $250 to lower-income Singapore Citizens, aged 30 and above, who have developed severe disability and are not able to benefit from CareShield Life, ElderShield and Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE), and have low MediSave balances and inadequate personal savings to meet their long-term care needs.

details.heading: What assessment is needed
details.body: To qualify for severe disability schemes, you need to be assessed by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor. The assessment must find that you are unable to perform three or more of the six Activities of Daily Living.

quotes.text: Additional Premium Support (APS) provides financial assistance to members who are unable to afford their premiums even after premium subsidies and MediSave use, and have limited family support.

title.full: Why long term care cover matters

summary.text: CareShield Life and ElderShield provide basic financial protection when long-term care needs and costs are uncertain.

details.heading: More people may need care
details.body: As Singapore's population ages, more people may need long-term care. One in two Singaporeans who are healthy at age 65 is expected to develop severe disability by the end of their lives.

details.heading: Care needs can last years
details.body: The length of severe disability and the cost of care can vary. The expected median duration is around four years, but three in 10 people remain severely disabled for 10 years or more.

details.heading: Families may not manage alone
details.body: Shrinking family sizes make it harder to rely only on personal and family savings to pay for long-term care.

details.heading: Insurance works with other support
details.body: These insurance schemes complement Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support.

quotes.text: Long-term care insurance schemes like CareShield Life and ElderShield help Singaporeans to pool their risks together within their cohort so that each Singaporean within that cohort has basic financial protection against the uncertainty and variability of the cost of long-term care.
The need for long-term care will rise as Singapore's population ages. One in two Singaporeans who are healthy at age 65 is expected to develop severe disability by the end of their lives.
The expected median duration for which individuals with severe disability remain in disability is around four years, but three in 10 remain in severe disability for 10 years or more.

Variation in the duration of severe disability and the accompanying costs of long-term care, coupled with shrinking family sizes in Singapore, make it increasingly challenging to rely solely on personal and family savings to pay for one's long-term care needs.
They complement other long-term care financing sources, such as Government subsidies, Government assistance schemes, community support, personal savings and family support.

steps.name: Check the date
steps.text: Check that the death was on or after 29 May 2022, and that less than 30 days have passed since the death or the issue of a new certificate.

steps.name: Check the details
steps.text: Check the identification number and document number. For a death certificate, use the deceased's identification number. For a stillbirth certificate, use the mother's identification number. The number must match the hospital or doctor's record.

steps.name: Try again later
steps.text: If the details are correct, try downloading the certificate again after 24 hours.

steps.name: Use another document
steps.text: While waiting, ask the hospital or doctor for a Confirmation of Death, Confirmation of Stillbirth, or NEHR printout document. These can be accepted for funeral arrangements, burial, and cremation.

steps.name: Submit a query
steps.text: If you still cannot download the certificate after 24 hours, submit a query.
